title: EnGenius Wi-Fi 7 AP $152.15 Delivered @ ENGENIUS NETWORKS SG Amazon AU
body:
Deal: EnGenius Wi-Fi 7 AP $152.15 Delivered @ ENGENIUS NETWORKS SG Amazon AU

[Ezekiel2320] Cloud Managed for Effortless Control
This would make it a non-starter for me personally
[internet-stranger] Why? It’s only the config that’s in the cloud.
No transmitted data leaves the local network.
Not that there is anything wrong with that stance, just curious.
[ad62623] I feel the same, it just seems unnecessary. How long should this device last, as long as the company feels like paying for their cloud services?
[Ezekiel2320] I've never heard of this brand before so did some looking. It appears they do generally have a standard configuration webui accessible inside the network which should let you do basic configuration without the app (ick²).
Not exposing the remote management interface to the internet removes this risk entirely*
*Insofar as trusting the firmware not to have exploits in it, which as we've seen in the news over the years, is almost all of them
[internet-stranger] @Ezekiel2320: EnGenius are much bigger in the business space and the US.
I haven’t tried the local web UI but a quick google says one exists on some models (not sure if that includes this model).
Another option would be configure via the cloud then block access. The APs keep the config and work without having to connect.
[internet-stranger] @internet-stranger: Not sure why the down votes. :(
Happy to have a discussion :)
[Ezekiel2320] https://www.vulncheck.com/advisories/engenius-enshare-iot-gi…
An OS command injection vulnerability exists in EnGenius EnShare Cloud Service version 1.4.11 and earlier. The usbinteract.cgi script fails to properly sanitize user input passed to the path parameter, allowing unauthenticated remote attackers to inject arbitrary shell commands. The injected commands are executed with root privileges, leading to full system compromise.
I just don't see the value of a "cloud management portal" on my router versus the risk of allowing an intruder into my house
[internet-stranger] Have fun throwing Unifi and Tplink in there :)
That was also patched long ago.
[internet-stranger] @internet-stranger: Not sure why the downvotes.
Old CVE that’s been patched by Engenius or a current unpatched one with Ubiquiti??
https://www.vulncheck.com/advisories/ubiquiti-unifi-devices-…
[reloxation] OP why you shilling this random brand so hard
[id] engenius have been around since the 90's!
[tephra] I have three of these:
Performance is ok, its tri-band AND it lets you mesh over 6Ghz which is useful to keep 5ghz free for devices.
The cloud management is a bit naff, completely unnecessary and you lose features if you dont pay like $15 a year, and its also a real pain to buy that license because they keep redirecting you to another website which you cant buy it from - not sure whats going on there.
Also, whenever you make a config change it drops all the wifi, which for some changes is just unnecessary.
I probably wouldn't recommend for a non-IT person.
I am hoping OpenWRT cracks root on it and publishes an image for it, then we get the best of both worlds…
